questions.q: A 28-year-old presents with a single well-defined hypopigmented anesthetic patch on the forearm. Skin biopsy shows non-caseating granulomas encasing nerve twigs. Slit-skin smear is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) presents with a single well-defined anesthetic hypopigmented patch, enlarged peripheral nerves, and negative smear. Biopsy shows granulomas encasing or destroying nerve twigs. BT has similar features but with more lesions.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman has painful oral ulcers for 3 months followed by flaccid blisters on the trunk. Nikolsky sign is positive. Histology shows suprabasal acantholysis with a 'row of tombstones' at the base. Which antibody is primarily responsible?
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris with mucosal involvement is caused by antibodies against desmoglein 3. Mucocutaneous type has both anti-Dsg3 and anti-Dsg1. Anti-BP180/BP230 are seen in bullous pemphigoid.

questions.q: A 22-year-old has her fourth episode of grouped vesicles on an erythematous base on the lip in 12 months. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. Which regimen best prevents recurrences?
opts: Acyclovir 200 mg five times daily for 5 days at onset
Famciclovir 500 mg three times daily for 7 days
Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV for severe episodes
questions.exp: Suppressive (continuous) therapy with valacyclovir 500 mg once daily is indicated for frequent recurrent HSV labialis (≥6 episodes/year) and significantly reduces recurrence frequency and severity.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man has a painless ulcer with indurated edges on the glans. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spirochetes. VDRL titer is 1:32. What is the treatment of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 14 days
questions.exp: Primary syphilis is treated with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM as a single dose. Doxycycline is reserved for penicillin-allergic patients. Azithromycin has documented resistance. Ceftriaxone is an alternative but not first-line.

questions.q: A 25-year-old athlete presents with scaling and pruritus between the toes and on the soles. KOH mount shows branching septate hyphae. What is the first-line topical treatment?
opts: Terbinafine 1% cream twice daily for 2 weeks
questions.exp: Terbinafine 1% cream is the preferred topical allylamine for tinea pedis caused by dermatophytes. Nystatin is ineffective against dermatophytes. Ciclopirox is effective but not first-line. Terbinafine has superior fungicidal activity.

questions.q: A 28-year-old woman has butterfly rash, photosensitivity, and joint pain. ANA is 1:160, complement is low, and proteinuria is present. Which antibody is most specific for systemic lupus erythematosus?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA antibodies are highly specific (~95%) for SLE and correlate with disease activity and lupus nephritis. Anti-Ro/La are more associated with Sjögren's syndrome. Anti-histone antibodies are characteristic of drug-induced lupus.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man has thick silvery-scaly plaques on the extensor surfaces of knees and elbows. Auspitz sign is positive and he has nail pitting. Which cytokines primarily drive the pathogenesis of psoriasis?
questions.exp: Psoriasis is primarily driven by Th1 and Th17 cells. IL-17A (from Th17 cells) and TNF-α are the dominant cytokines. The IL-23/Th17 axis is central to pathogenesis, which is why biologics targeting IL-17 (secukinumab, ixekizumab) and IL-23 (guselkumab) are effective.

questions.q: A 75-year-old patient develops tense blisters on erythematous skin over the trunk and flexures. Oral mucosa is uninvolved. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents in the elderly with tense blisters, negative Nikolsky sign, and sparing of mucosae. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the BMZ due to antibodies against BP180 and BP230. PV shows flaccid blisters with Nikolsky sign and mucosal involvement.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man with severe plaque psoriasis is started on methotrexate 15 mg weekly. After 2 months, he reports persistent nausea and oral sores. Which supplement reduces these adverse effects?
opts: Folic acid 5 mg daily (omit on methotrexate day)
questions.exp: Folic acid 5 mg daily (except the day of MTX) reduces mucosal and GI side effects of methotrexate by replenishing folate depleted by MTX's anti-folate mechanism, without significantly reducing efficacy. The dose is omitted on MTX day to avoid direct competition.

questions.q: A 5-year-old child presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth. There is no fever. What is the most common causative organism in non-bullous impetigo?
questions.exp: Staphylococcus aureus is currently the predominant cause of non-bullous impetigo, either alone or in mixed infections with Group A Streptococcus. Bullous impetigo is caused exclusively by S. aureus phage group II producing exfoliative toxin A.

questions.q: A 50-year-old presents with a pigmented lesion showing asymmetry, irregular border, and multiple colors (tan, brown, black). Dermoscopy reveals atypical pigment network and blue-white veil. What is the best diagnostic approach?
opts: Punch biopsy from the darkest area
questions.exp: For suspected melanoma, excisional biopsy with narrow (1–2 mm) clinical margins is the standard diagnostic approach. This preserves the full lesion for accurate Breslow thickness and histological staging. Shave biopsy risks transecting the lesion; punch biopsy may miss the deepest part.

questions.q: A 30-year-old presents with intensely pruritic grouped vesicles on elbows, knees, and buttocks. DIF shows granular IgA deposits in the dermal papillae. Duodenal biopsy confirms villous atrophy. Which dietary modification is therapeutic?
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is the cutaneous manifestation of celiac disease. A strict gluten-free diet leads to remission of both the skin disease and enteropathy. Dapsone controls skin lesions quickly but the gluten-free diet is the definitive treatment.

questions.q: A male patient receiving MDT for lepromatous leprosy develops fever, crops of tender erythematous nodules on the forearms and thighs, and painful eyes. Biopsy of the nodule shows neutrophilic infiltrate. What is the drug of choice for this reaction?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL, Type 2 leprosy reaction) is best managed with thalidomide (100–300 mg/day) in non-pregnant males, as it inhibits TNF-α. Prednisolone is used when thalidomide is contraindicated (e.g., women of childbearing age). MDT should never be stopped.

questions.q: A 65-year-old presents with a slowly enlarging, pearly, rolled-edge nodule with telangiectasias and central ulceration on the ala nasi. Excision margins are crucial. Which treatment offers the highest cure rate for this high-risk location?
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery offers the highest cure rate (≥99%) for basal cell carcinoma, especially at high-risk sites (H-zone of the face including nose, ears, eyelids). Real-time 100% margin evaluation prevents recurrence while conserving maximal normal tissue.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman has Raynaud's phenomenon, skin tightening limited to fingers and face, telangiectasias, and dysphagia. ANA shows a centromere staining pattern. Which subtype does she have?
questions.exp: Limited cutaneous SSc (CREST: Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia) is characterized by skin fibrosis distal to elbows/knees, anti-centromere antibodies, and a relatively better prognosis. Diffuse SSc has proximal skin involvement and anti-Scl-70.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child has recurrent intensely pruritic eczematous patches on the face and antecubital fossae. IgE is elevated at 450 IU/mL. For mild disease inadequately controlled with emollients, what is the first-line non-steroidal topical agent?
questions.exp: Pimecrolimus 1% cream is a calcineurin inhibitor indicated as first-line non-steroidal option for mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis in children ≥2 years, particularly on the face and skin folds. Tacrolimus 0.03% is approved for ≥2 years but is second-line for moderate-to-severe disease.

questions.q: A 25-year-old develops depigmented, chalk-white patches on the hands and face over 2 years. Wood's lamp accentuates the depigmentation. Which pathomechanism is primarily responsible for vitiligo?
opts: Autoimmune cytotoxic T-cell destruction of melanocytes
Excess melanin transfer blockade at the dendrite tips
questions.exp: Vitiligo is primarily an autoimmune condition. CD8+ cytotoxic T-cells, activated by autoantigens (tyrosinase, MART-1), selectively destroy melanocytes. Serum anti-melanocyte antibodies are also found. This is why JAK inhibitors (ruxolitinib cream) targeting the IFN-γ pathway are effective.

questions.q: A 20-year-old man has purulent urethral discharge and dysuria for 4 days. Gram stain of the discharge shows Gram-negative diplococci inside polymorphonuclear cells. What is the current recommended treatment per WHO/CDC guidelines?
opts: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg orally as a single dose
Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM as a single dose
Azithromycin 1 g orally as a single dose
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days
questions.exp: Due to widespread fluoroquinolone resistance, ceftriaxone 500 mg IM as a single dose is now the recommended monotherapy for uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea per updated CDC 2021 guidelines (previously 250 mg). Azithromycin as monotherapy is not recommended due to emerging resistance.

questions.q: A patient started on carbamazepine 3 weeks ago develops fever, skin pain, and blistering with >30% BSA detachment, plus oral and conjunctival erosions. What is the single most critical immediate step?
questions.exp: Immediate discontinuation of the causative drug is the single most important step in toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN). Early withdrawal significantly improves mortality. All other interventions (IVIG, cyclosporine, burn unit care) are secondary to stopping the drug immediately.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with violaceous periorbital edema (heliotrope rash), flat erythematous papules over the knuckles (Gottron's papules), and progressive proximal muscle weakness. Which investigation best quantifies muscle damage?
questions.exp: Serum creatine kinase (CK) is the most useful marker of active muscle inflammation in dermatomyositis. Levels correlate with disease activity and response to treatment. ANA is often positive but non-specific. Anti-Jo-1 is the most common myositis-specific antibody.

questions.q: Patch tests applied to the back are read at 48 and 96 hours. At 96 hours, a site shows erythema, infiltration, and discrete vesicles confined to the test site. How is this graded per ICDRG criteria?
opts: +++ (extreme positive): coalescing bullae with intense erythema
IR (irritant reaction): follicular papules or pustules
questions.exp: ICDRG grading: ? = doubtful (faint macular erythema); + = weak positive (erythema + infiltration ± papules); ++ = strong positive (erythema + infiltration + papules + vesicles); +++ = extreme positive (coalescing vesicles/bullae). Discrete vesicles with erythema = ++ (strong positive).

questions.q: A 22-year-old man has multiple hypopigmented, finely scaly macules on the chest and upper back. KOH mount shows short hyphae and round spores ('spaghetti and meatballs'). What is the first-line topical treatment?
opts: Selenium sulfide 2.5% lotion applied for 10 minutes daily for 2 weeks
questions.exp: Pityriasis (tinea) versicolor due to Malassezia furfur is best treated topically with selenium sulfide 2.5% or ketoconazole shampoo/cream for mild-to-moderate cases. Terbinafine has poor activity against Malassezia. Oral fluconazole is reserved for extensive or recurrent disease.

questions.q: A 65-year-old diabetic presents with painful vesicular eruption along the right V1 dermatome. A vesicle is also noted on the tip of the nose (Hutchinson's sign). What complication must be urgently evaluated?
opts: Herpes zoster ophthalmicus with corneal involvement
questions.exp: Hutchinson's sign (vesicle on nose tip) indicates involvement of the nasociliary branch of V1, which also supplies the eyeball. This predicts a high risk of herpes zoster ophthalmicus with corneal keratitis, uveitis, or acute retinal necrosis. Urgent ophthalmological evaluation is mandatory.

questions.q: On histology of normal skin, which epidermal layer is characterized by a single row of columnar cells perpendicular to the basement membrane, containing the highest mitotic activity?
questions.exp: The stratum basale (germinativum) is the single innermost layer of columnar or cuboidal cells attached to the basement membrane zone. It contains keratinocyte stem cells and mitotically active progenitors. Melanocytes, Merkel cells, and Langerhans cells are also found here and in the spinosum.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with a painful genital ulcer with soft, undermined, ragged edges and unilateral tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Gram stain shows 'school of fish' Gram-negative coccobacilli. What is the treatment of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 MU IM single dose
Azithromycin 1 g orally as a single dose
Tetracycline 500 mg four times daily for 7 days
Metronidazole 400 mg three times daily for 7 days
questions.exp: Chancroid (caused by Haemophilus ducreyi) is characterized by a painful soft ulcer with ragged undermined edges and tender suppurative inguinal lymphadenopathy. Azithromycin 1 g orally as a single dose is the preferred treatment due to efficacy and compliance. Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM is an equivalent alternative.

questions.q: A 70-year-old farmer has an indurated, keratinizing, ulcerating lesion on the lower lip. Biopsy confirms invasive well-differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. Which feature most significantly increases the risk of local recurrence and metastasis?
opts: Tumor thickness greater than 2 mm and perineural invasion
questions.exp: High-risk features for SCC include: tumor thickness >2 mm, perineural invasion (PNI), poor differentiation, size >2 cm, location on the lip/ear, and immunosuppression. Perineural invasion is particularly associated with local recurrence and regional metastasis and requires wide excision/MMS plus adjuvant radiotherapy.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with recurrent wheals lasting 4–8 hours accompanied by angioedema for 10 weeks. No identifiable trigger. What is the first-line pharmacological treatment for chronic spontaneous urticaria?
opts: Oral prednisolone 0.5 mg/kg daily for 2 weeks
questions.exp: Second-generation non-sedating H1-antihistamines (cetirizine, loratadine, fexofenadine, bilastine) are first-line for chronic spontaneous urticaria per EAACI/GA2LEN guidelines. Dose can be increased up to 4× before stepping up. Omalizumab is third-line. Steroids are not recommended for long-term use.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man and his wife both complain of severe nocturnal pruritus with burrow-like lesions in the finger webs, wrists, nipples, and genitalia. Which oral single-dose treatment has the highest efficacy for scabies?
opts: Benzyl benzoate 25% lotion applied for 24 hours
Ivermectin 200 mcg/kg orally as a single dose (repeat at 2 weeks)
questions.exp: Oral ivermectin 200 mcg/kg as a single dose (repeated at 2 weeks) is highly effective for scabies and is especially useful in outbreaks, immunocompromised patients, and Norwegian (crusted) scabies. Permethrin 5% cream is the most effective topical agent. Lindane is neurotoxic and largely abandoned.

questions.q: A 55-year-old diabetic presents with thickened, discolored, crumbling toenails for 2 years. PAS stain of nail clippings confirms dermatophyte onychomycosis involving all 10 toenails. What is the most effective systemic treatment?
opts: Fluconazole 150 mg once weekly for 6 months
Itraconazole 200 mg twice daily for 1 week per month for 3 pulse cycles
questions.exp: Terbinafine 250 mg daily for 12 weeks (toenails) or 6 weeks (fingernails) achieves the highest mycological cure rates (70–80%) for dermatophyte onychomycosis. It is fungicidal and has excellent nail penetration. Itraconazole pulse therapy is a second-line option. Griseofulvin has lower cure rates.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with 10-year history of plaque psoriasis develops asymmetric oligoarthritis of DIP joints. X-ray shows 'pencil-in-cup' deformity consistent with psoriatic arthritis mutilans. He fails methotrexate. Which biologic specifically inhibits IL-17A?
questions.exp: Secukinumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody that selectively targets IL-17A, which is pivotal in both psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. It is approved for both conditions. Ustekinumab targets the p40 subunit of IL-12/23. Adalimumab is anti-TNF-α. Ixekizumab is another anti-IL-17A agent.
